newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian markets surge on Wall Street, local listings.
newsitem.headline: Asian markets surge on Wall Street, local listings.

text.p: Asian markets soared on Monday, with Hong Kong and Australia shooting to record closes on Wall Street's lead and Jakarta soaring 2.5 percent on the listing of a giant state-owned bank.
Friday's surge on Wall Street also helped Tokyo post moderate gains.
On the downside, Seoul shares plunged more than two percent, while New Zealanders shrugged off Wall Street to close more than half a percent lower.
The Dow Jones Industrial average closed 53.29 points higher on Friday at 6,471.76, the 42nd record closing high for 1996.
The U.S. surge and continued bullish sentiment in the property market led Hong Kong shares to a record close on Monday. The Hang Seng Index ended 122.60 points or 0.93 percent higher at 13,239.39.
"Obviously it is on the back of New York on Friday," said Miles Remington, sales trader at Crosby Securities.
"Property is still the main word in Hong Kong's stock market at the moment," he added.
Tokyo stocks were lifted in the morning by the record close on Wall Street, coupled with the biggest gain this year in London on Friday.

Brokers added, however, the key Nikkei benchmark was likely to remain boxed in a range until a key business sentiment survey comes out later this week. At the close, the Nikkei was up 77.46 points or 0.37 percent at 21,293.57.
Australian shares finished at a record close, bolstered by the Dow's continued strength. The All Ordinaries index closed 11.3 points or 0.47 percent higher at 2,394.7.
New Zealand missed Wall Street's cue. The NZSE-40 capital index declining 0.55 percent to close at 2,339.17.
In Jakarta, giant state-owned Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) was listed locally after one of the country's best-received floats, sending the index leaping ahead.
The index closed 2.51 percent higher at 628.24 points on a sharp inflow of funds after BNI's listing, brokers said.

"It was widely expected that the BNI listing would enliven Jakarta stocks. I think it (the boom) will last until the second week of December before the market slows down for the Christmas holiday," a foreign broker said.

Kuala Lumpur blue chips extended their reach into new high ground for 1996, gaining 0.63 percent as money continued to pour into larger-capitalisation shares. The Composite Index tacked on 7.66 points to close at 1,225.62.
Taiwan's financial sector stole the limelight from electronics to post sharp gains, driving the market to another 22-month high amid what one broker called "extreme bullishness".
The weighted index ended up 96.71 points or 1.41 percent at 6,938.87, the highest since January 1, 1995.
In Seoul, stocks closed at this year's lowest level as jitters over share oversupply and a bribery scandal involving the head of a leading commercial bank dampened sentiment.
The composite stock index shed 2.05 percent or 14.99 points to a provisional close of 716.45.
On Saturday, state prosecutors said they had arrested Sohn Hong-gyun, president of SEOULBANK, the country's sixth-biggest bank, on bribery charges.
Thai stocks closed 0.26 percent lower on continued uncertainty about the shape of a new Thai cabinet being formed by coalition leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, brokers said.

Bombay shares rebounded 1.20 percent on Monday after plunging nearly four percent in early trade. Singapore's Straits Times Industrials Index ended up 0.50 percent at 2,205.69. Manila shares ended mixed.
Brent crude futures were untraded by late trading in Asia.
January Brent futures were quoted on SIMEX at $23.04/$23.15 per barrel at 0920 GMT, just above the London settlement of $23.03 and higher than earlier quotes of $22.90/$23.00.
Hong Kong gold ended at $374.90/375.40 an ounce against Hong Kong's Saturday close at $376.30/80 and New York's $376.10/60 close on Friday.
The dollar got a boost against the yen in late Tokyo trade from comments by a Bank of Japan official, which invited fresh concerns over the Japanese financial industry.
At 10:23 GMT the dollar traded at 112.45/50 yen and 1.5144/48 marks.
